name: Summerstrand
tagline: The beachfront suburb, with the university and the boardwalk
description: The coastal suburb east of the centre, running along Hobie Beach and Kings Beach with a boardwalk, restaurants and the Nelson Mandela University campus behind. It is the most comfortable and secure part of the city, where most foreigners and students live, and where the beach is walkable.
bestFor: Almost anyone arriving, for the beach access and the relative security
pros: Beaches and the boardwalk on the doorstep
The most comfortable area to walk in daylight
cons: The highest rents in the city
Still requires the usual South African caution after dark

name: Richmond Hill
tagline: The restaurant quarter, restored Victorian terraces
description: An inner suburb above the harbour that has been substantially restored over the last decade, with Stanley Street now holding the best concentration of restaurants and bars in the city. Housing is Victorian terraces and semis, and it sits within reach of both the centre and the beachfront.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting the restaurant scene and period housing
pros: The best restaurants and bars in the city
Central position between the harbour and the beach
cons: Property crime remains a real concern
Limited parking on the narrow streets

name: Central and the Donkin Reserve
tagline: The old town on the hill above the port
description: The historic centre around the Donkin Reserve, with its lighthouse and pyramid, and Route 67, a public art walk of sixty-seven works commemorating Mandela's years of service. The Victorian and Edwardian buildings are the city's architectural inheritance, some restored and many not.
bestFor: Stays that want the city's history and are content with a mixed area
pros: Route 67 and the historic quarter on the doorstep
Views over the port and the bay
cons: Uneven, with genuine neglect alongside restoration
Requires real caution, particularly after dark

name: Walmer
tagline: The established leafy suburb near the airport
description: A settled residential suburb west of Summerstrand, with older houses on large plots, mature trees and good schools, sitting beside the airport, which is unusually close to the city here. It is quiet, comfortable and the standard choice for families, with the beach ten minutes away by car.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a house with a garden and airport proximity
pros: Large houses and gardens at moderate rents
cons: Ten minutes by car to the beach

name: Addo and the Sundays River (60 km north)
tagline: Out at the elephant park, in the citrus valley
description: The farming country around Addo Elephant National Park, an hour inland, with guesthouses and lodges among citrus orchards along the Sundays River. The park is malaria-free and holds elephants in numbers plus lion, buffalo and rhino. It is a rural base rather than an urban one.
bestFor: Stays built around the park rather than the city
pros: Addo Elephant National Park at the gate
cons: An hour from the city and a car is essential
Almost no services beyond the lodges
Connectivity is weaker than in the city
